assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hardware correction of spherical aberration made sub-angstrom, atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy routine in transmission electron microscopy. It is a genuine invention that opened a door to structure and chemistry people could not see before, and it underpins work across materials, catalysis, interfaces and quantum materials. Originality is high because it overcame the long-standing Scherzer-theorem limitation. From my own field I can attest to its practical impact.
assessment.attribution: The correctors were designed by Rose and built and demonstrated by Haider (TEM, with Rose and Uhlemann) and by Urban with Haider and colleagues, and Urban led the first demonstrations on materials. The three credited names map onto the decisive theory, construction and first-application steps. I recall that other groups (for example Krivanek and colleagues on the STEM side) also contributed, and that is not in the supplied list, so I cannot call the allocation fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Results were independently confirmed by commercial instruments installed worldwide for roughly two decades; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM corrector work (Krivanek and collaborators) needs to be weighed against the TEM correctors, which would complicate the three-person configuration.
Exact division of credit between theory (Rose) and implementation (Haider, Urban) is from my memory of the record and not independently verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson at ATLAS and CMS in 2012 completed the Standard Model and is an unambiguous, verified discovery with a large effect on our understanding of nature. The 2013 prize recognized the theoretical prediction; the experimental discovery is the original observation and has never been recognized.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the hard part. Collaborations of thousands made the discovery, and the three credited names are founding leaders and spokespersons of the proposals rather than individuals who made the decisive measurement. The rules limit the prize to three persons, and there is a real risk that this does not reflect who did the original work. I would want the committee to be careful and not treat leadership as equivalent to discovery.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequent Run 2 coupling measurements; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether three individuals can fairly represent a collaboration-scale discovery.
Whether the instrumental and leadership roles of the credited names constitute the discovery in the sense of the statutes.
Additional deserving individuals (e.g. analysis and detector leaders) are not in the supplied credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane. It is a new window on the universe built through an instrument, which fits what I regard as an original experimental discovery with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is widely seen as the driving force of the IceCube concept and construction and Spiering as a long-time leader in neutrino telescopes (AMANDA/Baikal lineage). The two-person configuration is clean, but earlier pioneers of the field (e.g. DUMAND, Baikal) are not in the supplied list, and the contribution of the collaboration is large.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux is robustly established and several source associations have appeared, though source identification is still developing; timing is reasonable but arguably slightly early for source claims.
uncertainties: Source association evidence (NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056) is at moderate significance and needs more confirmation.
Credit relative to earlier detector pioneers and the broader collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and Ye's experimental realization with strontium, brought clock accuracy to the 10^-18 level and enabled tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. It is a new measurement tool with clear impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and both groups demonstrated the clock experimentally. The two-person list looks defensible, though the 2005 prize already recognised Hall and Hansch for the frequency comb, which Ye used, and other lattice-clock groups (e.g. Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow) are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories with steady improvement; the technique is mature. The redefinition of the second is pending, which makes timing sensible but not urgent.
uncertainties: How the committee views overlap with the frequency-comb prize.
Priority between the original proposal and early experimental demonstrations by other groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance (1995) and the later giant effect in MgO-based magnetic tunnel junctions led to the read heads of hard disks and to MRAM. These are experimental discoveries with large societal impact that complement the 2007 prize on giant magnetoresistance. Both the original observation and the improvement matter for the application.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported reproducible room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Parkin and the Yuasa/Djayaprawira groups reported the coherent MgO-based effect in 2004. The list gives a plausible three-person configuration, but Yuasa and the Julliere low-temperature work (1975) are not in it, so the allocation between the original observation and the later improvement is a real question.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and in devices; the interpretation (coherent tunnelling through MgO) is stable. Recognition is timely given that it follows the GMR prize.
uncertainties: Priority between Moodera/Miyazaki (original room-temperature TMR) and Parkin/Yuasa (MgO).
Julliere's 1975 result and Yuasa's contribution are outside the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, produced by simply controlling a twist angle. It is a prediction followed by an original, clearly demonstrated experiment. As a microscopist I find the combination of theory and direct measurement convincing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle (2011) and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experiments in 2018. The credit allocation appears natural, but other experimental groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yazdani, Kim) contributed later and the fraction of relevant credit is open.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the field is still moving quickly, the nature of the superconductivity is not settled, and sample variability is a concern. This is possibly premature.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample variability remain unresolved.
Whether the discovery is mature enough for a prize now, only about eight years after the experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser (1994) is a real invention: a unipolar semiconductor laser based on engineered intersubband transitions in a superlattice, which gives tunable mid-infrared and terahertz sources. It is widely used in spectroscopy, gas sensing and security, so impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: The first device was reported by Faist, Capasso, Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson and Cho at Bell Labs. Capasso led the concept and Faist did the key experiment, while Cho's molecular-beam epitaxy was essential. The relative merit of Cho versus Sirtori or Sivco is an open question, and the 1971 Kazarinov-Suris proposal is a prior idea not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and commercialised; interpretation is stable. Recognition has been long awaited.
uncertainties: Priority of the Kazarinov-Suris proposal and the role of Sirtori, Sivco and Hutchinson.
Whether epitaxial growth (Cho) should be credited as decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new class of materials with protected edge and surface states, first predicted by Kane and Mele and observed in HgTe quantum wells. The conceptual impact is large, and the experimental verification was clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction in 2005, and Molenkamp's group delivered the original experimental observation in 2007 after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not in the supplied list, and I recall that Shoucheng Zhang died in 2018, so a fair three-person allocation is open. Experiments in 3D materials (Hasan, Cava, Kane-Fu-Mele) also complicate the picture.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed experimentally and theoretically, with extensive follow-up; recognition is plausible but only after resolving credit between 2D and 3D discoveries.
uncertainties: Credit for the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and for 3D topological insulator experiments is not in the credited names.
Whether the prize should centre on 2D quantum spin Hall or on 3D topological insulators.
